questions_json.question: What usually happens to equity valuations when a central bank aggressively hikes repo rates?
options: Equities experience valuation compression due to higher discounting rates
Stock prices universally soar due to higher bank deposit margins
There is zero correlation between interest rates and equity multiples
Commodities immediately plunge to absolute zero
questions_json.explanation: Higher discount rates lower the present value of future cash flows, compressing valuation multiples.

questions_json.question: What primary benchmark index does the RBI monitor for targeting headline retail inflation?
questions_json.explanation: The RBI legally targets CPI Combined with an anchor band of 4% (+/- 2%).

questions_json.question: If the Indian Rupee depreciates against the US Dollar, which sector benefits the most?
questions_json.explanation: Export businesses invoice in USD while operating expenses are in INR, widening operating margins.

questions_json.question: What does a high Price-to-Earnings (P/E) ratio relative to historical averages generally signify?
options: The company is on the verge of bankruptcy
The market is paying a premium in anticipation of strong future earnings growth
The company yields the highest dividends in its peer group
questions_json.explanation: Elevated P/E indicates high investor willingness to pay for anticipated growth.

questions_json.question: What is the primary role of market-wide circuit breakers on NSE/BSE?
options: To permanently shut down weak listed companies
To temporarily halt trading during flash shocks and curb contagion panic
To give institutional desks extra margin limits
To artificially peg end-of-day closing prices
questions_json.explanation: Circuit breakers act as cooling periods to digest market information during sharp volatility.

questions_json.question: Which metric measures a stock volatility relative to the benchmark index (Nifty 50)?
questions_json.explanation: Beta represents systematic sensitivity; Beta > 1 implies higher volatility than the benchmark.

rounds.name: Round 0: Initial Purchase Session
rounds.description: Initial stock purchase from predetermined universe of ~50 stocks. Unlimited supply from Econ desk.
rounds.rules_note: Mandatory 60% Deployment: Each team must invest at least ₹6,00,000 in this session. Unspent cash carries forward.

rounds.name: Round 1: Inter-Team Trading
rounds.description: First floor trading session. Teams negotiate and execute trades mutually using physical signed trade slips.
rounds.rules_note: Live price uses quantity-weighted average of latest 3 trades. End-of-round cash check: minimum ₹1,00,000 required.

rounds.name: Round 2: Inter-Team Trading
rounds.description: Trading continues under Round 2 opening prices after News 2 and R% adjustments.
rounds.rules_note: Trading via signed trade slips. Binding agreement once signed. End-of-round cash floor: ₹1,00,000.

rounds.name: IPO Round 1: Tech Unicorn Primary Offering
rounds.description: Primary market offering. Teams submit lot demand; smooth listing formula determines post-IPO price.
rounds.rules_note: Smooth Listing Formula: P_listing = P0 × (0.7 + 0.6S/(1+S)). Undersubscribed IPO gives every requesting team 1 lot.

rounds.name: Round 3: Multi-Sector Expansion & IPO Trading
rounds.description: Secondary floor trading resumes, now including newly listed IPO 1 stock.
rounds.rules_note: 5% dual brokerage on P2P trades. Quantity-weighted 3-trade rolling price rule active.

rounds.name: IPO Round 2: Green Energy Conglomerate Offering
rounds.description: Second primary market IPO window. Teams submit lot applications.
rounds.rules_note: Listing price determined by aggregate subscription ratio S = D / L.

rounds.name: Round 4: High Beta Floor Trading
rounds.description: High volatility secondary trading session with breaking news adjustments.
rounds.rules_note: Valid slips received by round cutoff processed after close to establish next price base.

rounds.name: Round 5: Final Trading & Closing Bell
rounds.description: Final Dalal Street trading window. Unexecuted slips discarded at close. Closing prices determine final winner.
rounds.rules_note: Final Portfolio Value = Cash + Σ(Holdings × Round 5 Close). Teams below ₹1,00,000 cash face round disqualification.
